summary.name: SRE methods and climate change
summary.one_liner: A blog post explaining how Site Reliability Engineering concepts (SLIs, SLOs, error budgets) can be applied to measure and reduce the climate impact of software services, using power-consumption metrics from Scaphandre.
use_cases: defining SLIs and SLOs for energy or emissions
measuring power consumption of servers and services
estimating ghg emissions per request or per user
explaining sre and devops differences to a team
building error budget dashboards for product and engineering teams
summary.what_it_does: The post introduces SRE and DevOps principles, then explains Service Level Indicators (ratios of good events to total events), Service Level Objectives, and error budgets as ways to balance velocity and reliability. It proposes extending reliability to include climate impact, arguing services should not jeopardize future emissions goals. It names Scaphandre, an open-source lightweight monitoring daemon for power consumption metrics that exports to Prometheus and Riemann, and suggests combining it with the co2signal API to estimate GHG emissions. It closes with example emissions-based SLOs, described by the author as arbitrary.
notable: Applies SLI/SLO and error budget concepts to carbon and energy metrics
Scaphandre open-source power consumption monitoring daemon named as the measurement tool
Example SLOs such as per-request emissions thresholds and per-user power caps
caveats: The example SLO numbers are explicitly described by the author as arbitrary
Scaphandre is described as storing data in Prometheus and Riemann, with Warp10 support said to be coming soon
Hardware and manufacturing emissions are hard to measure and are not covered by the power-based approach
